evidence: canvas_integration/main.py:sync_module_structure() is a pure delegation to upload_module_to_canvas() with zero added policy — a one-liner wrapper that serves no purpose distinguishable from a direct alias.

format_conversion/utils.py:convert_markdown_to_pdf() calls render_markdown_to_pdf(str(input_path), str(output_path)) with only string coercions — no error handling, no config policy, no translation logic added.
format_conversion/utils.py:convert_audio_to_text() calls transcribe_audio(str(input_path), str(output_path)) — same pure-forward pattern.
module_organization/utils.py:check_file_exists() wraps file_path.exists() and file_path.is_file() in a named function with a docstring — adds no domain policy over two boolean operators.
module_organization/utils.py:check_directory_exists() is analogous — thin stdlib wrap with no domain value.
module_organization/utils.py:ensure_directory_exists() wraps directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) — a one-liner re-exported under a domain name.

lab_manual/utils.py:read_markdown_file() and html_website/utils.py:read_markdown_file() are near-identical implementations of the same function, duplicating the file-read+not-exists-check pattern across modules instead of centralizing it.

markdown_to_pdf/utils.py:read_markdown_file(), lab_manual/utils.py:read_markdown_file(), html_website/utils.py:read_markdown_file() — three independent near-identical implementations of the same one-level-up utility across three modules.

ensure_output_directory() appears in at least five modules (batch_processing, lab_manual, html_website, markdown_to_pdf, text_to_speech, format_conversion) as near-identical path.mkdir() one-liners — a generic helper surface repeated across bounded packages rather than centralized.

file_validation/utils.py exposes validate_assignment_name(), validate_lecture_name(), validate_lab_name(), validate_study_guide_name(), validate_quiz_name() — each is a one-liner wrapping matches_pattern() with a specific config constant; the indirection adds no value over direct config.PATTERN.match() calls at the caller side.

format_conversion/utils.py defines both get_output_path() (takes Path, returns Path) and get_conversion_path() (takes str, returns str) — two functions for the same semantic operation with different type signatures, creating dual generic entry points.

strengths: Module-level __init__.py files act as proper public facades, re-exporting a curated subset of main.py symbols rather than leaking all internals.
canvas_integration/utils.py:make_canvas_request() is a legitimate wrapper — it adds auth header injection and rate-limit delay, justifying its existence.
batch_processing/main.py and scripts/generate_all_outputs.py form a clean two-layer: scripts orchestrate, main.py owns domain logic, no back-and-forth hop through unnecessary intermediaries.
lab_manual/utils.py defines rich domain objects (TableConfig, MeasurementConfig, LabElement) with dataclasses rather than untyped dicts — good abstraction leverage.
abstraction_fitness.issue_character: The codebase systematically exposes thin one-liner delegations and duplicated micro-helpers across bounded packages instead of choosing between centralizing the shared utility or simply calling the underlying operation directly.
abstraction_fitness.score_rationale: The codebase sits in the middle range. Legitimate abstractions exist (auth wrappers, domain dataclasses, facade __init__ modules). But there is a pervasive pattern of one-liner wrapper functions with no added policy — sync_module_structure delegating to upload_module_to_canvas, five independent ensure_output_directory() implementations, three read_markdown_file() clones, and a chain of single-dispatch validator wrappers in file_validation/utils.py. These raise the indirection cost without buying any leverage, placing the score below the 70s but above the 50s due to the codebase's overall direct module topology.

issues.summary: sync_module_structure() is a pure delegation to upload_module_to_canvas() with no added policy
evidence: Lines 123-146: function validates path, then calls return upload_module_to_canvas(module_path, canvas_course_id, api_key, domain) with a comment 'For now, we'll use the upload function'
issues.suggestion: Remove sync_module_structure() and expose upload_module_to_canvas() directly, or implement distinct sync semantics (idempotent upsert vs replace) that justify a separate name.

issues.summary: convert_markdown_to_pdf() and convert_audio_to_text() are pure argument-forwarding wrappers
evidence: convert_markdown_to_pdf(): entire body is render_markdown_to_pdf(str(input_path), str(output_path)) — only adds string coercions, no error handling or config
convert_audio_to_text(): entire body is transcribe_audio(str(input_path), str(output_path)) — same pattern
issues.suggestion: Either inline these at call sites in format_conversion/main.py or add actual boundary policy (error wrapping, format validation) to justify the wrapper layer.

issues.summary: ensure_output_directory() duplicated as identical one-liner across at least five modules
evidence: Each module defines ensure_output_directory() with body: output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) or directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
No module imports this utility from a shared location
issues.suggestion: Consolidate into one shared utility (e.g., src/publish/utils.py already has clean_directory — add ensure_output_directory there) and have modules import the shared version.

issues.summary: read_markdown_file() defined independently in three separate modules with near-identical logic
evidence: All three check file_path.exists(), raise FileNotFoundError, then return file_path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
html_website/utils.py imports markdown independently without reusing lab_manual or markdown_to_pdf utilities
issues.suggestion: Place read_markdown_file() in one module (markdown_to_pdf/utils.py is already used cross-module by format_conversion) and have lab_manual and html_website import from there.

issues.summary: Five single-dispatch validator functions in file_validation/utils.py each wrap matches_pattern() with a config constant
evidence: validate_assignment_name() body: return matches_pattern(file_name, config.ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN)
validate_lecture_name(), validate_lab_name(), validate_study_guide_name(), validate_quiz_name() follow identical pattern
matches_pattern() itself is a one-liner: return bool(pattern.match(name))
issues.suggestion: Collapse the chain: expose a single validate_file_name(file_name, file_type) function or let callers call config.PATTERN.match() directly; at minimum remove the matches_pattern() intermediate.

issues.summary: format_conversion/utils.py defines two functions for the same semantic operation with different type signatures
evidence: get_output_path(input_path: Path, output_format: str, output_dir: Optional[Path]) -> Path
get_conversion_path(input_path: str, output_format: str) -> str — same logic, string-typed
issues.suggestion: Remove get_conversion_path() and standardize on get_output_path() with Path types; callers needing strings can call str() at the boundary.

root_causes: Module-by-module scaffolding pattern created parallel utility layers in each package rather than shared infrastructure from the start
The ensure_output_directory and read_markdown_file pattern was copy-pasted as each new module was created
likely_symptoms: sync_module_structure — pure delegation with no distinguishing policy
matches_pattern — intermediate one-liner adds no value
